title: How Many Subsets Add Up to s

concept.title: Take it or leave it
body: For every number there are two choices: it is **in** the subset or **out**. A recursive function looks at the numbers one by one with the target that is **still missing**: `count(i, remaining)`. Taking `a[i]` lowers the missing amount, leaving it does not, and when all numbers have been decided, the subset is good exactly when nothing is missing.

All numbers are not negative, so as soon as `remaining` becomes negative it can never come back to 0, and the whole branch is cut. That **pruning** removes many of the `2^n` leaves. Subsets are told apart by the positions of their numbers: two equal values at different positions give different subsets.

statement: You are given `n` non-negative integers and a target `s`. Count the subsets (sets of positions, the empty set included) whose numbers add up to exactly `s`. The sum of the empty subset is 0.
inputFormat: The second line has the `n` integers.
hints: For every number you can take it or leave it: two recursive calls.
Pass the amount that is still missing; at the end it must be exactly 0.
A negative missing amount can never become 0 again (all numbers are not negative), so stop there.

explanation: `count(i, remaining)` decides number `i`: leave it, or take it and lower `remaining`. A negative `remaining` ends the branch; after the last number the subset counts if `remaining` is 0.
solution.complexity: Time O(2^n) in the worst case (all zeros), space O(n).
